The Central Dogma: DNA Encodes RNA; RNA Encodes Protein
The flow of genetic information in cells from DNA to mRNA to protein is described by the central
dogma (Figure 15.3), which states that genes specify the sequence of mRNAs, which in turn
specify the sequence of amino acids making up all proteins. The decoding of one molecule to
another is performed by specific proteins and RNAs. Because the information stored in DNA is so
central to cellular function, it makes intuitive sense that the cell would make mRNA copies of this
information for protein synthesis, while keeping the DNA itself intact and protected.
